verified_behaviors: Read-only organization/Volume discovery filters active leases and completed starts. Existing target bindings must match fully; atomic claims retain current authority, queue deadlines and dispatch rules.

PostgreSQL tests cover concurrent claim ownership, WAL restart, Observe-only recovery, all eight target fields, cancellation, revoked authority alongside another eligible request, and migration preservation.

The real daemon schedules two requests while their organization lock is held. SIGTERM stops discovery and joins both jobs after the barrier releases; both receipts commit. One preparation is new and the other recovers a real published directory without replacing its inode or contents.
Daemon restart schedules zero prepared requests. An expired dispatched request with missing publication remains Preparing/storage_unknown and its directory remains absent.

Independent SQL and filesystem reads verify all three preparation requests. Signed S3 reads verify five Artifact captures and their seven files; a separate readonly JuiceFS process verifies post-fence durable bytes.
The existing 17-case execution fixture, 18 authenticated output downloads, 36 S3 references and CSI/gVisor paths pass with the shared queue options and updated preparation helper.
experiment_notes: No repo-sandbox targets were registered; used the previously authorized disposable QEMU fallback with 4 vCPU, 6 GiB RAM and a 24 GiB overlay.

The first complete Candidate run passed the new queue scenarios but its old FUSE phase rejected root-owned symlinks deliberately left by earlier file-gateway negative tests. The fixture now verifies FUSE before those mutations; production fencing was unchanged.

A diagnostic rerun encountered an already retained Artifact spool from the first run. The final full run used fresh private cache/spool directories and passed. These failed attempts are not counted as successful checks.
The supervisor OCI image was reused after confirming its source-bound binary hash; it was unchanged in this increment.
limits: One Linux VM with isolated HTTP object transport; no production TLS, HA, cross-node, load or power-loss certification.
Concurrency 1-4 and polling 250-5000ms bound one process only. The live scenario verifies two scheduled jobs and shutdown while database claims wait; it is not a storage throughput benchmark.
Preflight and filesystem work remain joined. Synchronous log output or blocked IO can delay progress/shutdown. The example service timeout is not a physical IO guarantee.

An expired dispatched request is observed only; missing publication is not replayed. Permission loss and uncertain storage retain requests and reservations; no automatic cancellation or general drain recovery.
Computer ready=false; public execution unsupported. Volume orchestration, full lifecycle scheduling, runtime/App health, browser/ComputerView and T01-T43 product acceptance remain incomplete.
